comment: Great professor and makes AIS a pretty manageable class. Staying up to date on assignments is key, and most of the information for assignments can be found in the slides. She is always available by email or for office hours if you have trouble on the Excel assignments. Lots of the class is weighted away from exams.
Her excel hw is as difficult as hell and no one has enough time to complete/ask questions in class.

Dr. Austin is the best! Her tests are manageable if you stay on top of your work, her projects are informative, and she makes classtime a great experience. I dreaded taking AIS for years but my dread really was unwarranted - the class was great.

Dr. Austin exudes love for accounting. The AIS course focuses heavily on relevant topics, and she teaches with clarity and does a great job in answering questions in class and in office hours. She truly has her students' best interests at heart. There were a few tricky partner assignments throughout the course, but her quizzes and exams were fair.

I liked her as a professor. I get why people say she's a tough grader but she does a good job of giving you a lot of chances to earn points. There are 2 tests, 3 quizzes, a few group projects, and 1 homework assignment a week so even if you bomb a test you'll be okay. She wants her students to succeed and goes out of her way to make class engaging.

Prof Austin is incredible. She is very smart and really knows her stuff, but she teaches in a very informal and approachable manner. However, do not let her kindness make you think that she's easy. She will be fair in her exams, but you still need to be prepared when taking the exams. She will curve and is very understanding.
Enjoyed her class. Great professor and grades reasonably

Professor Austin is an amazing and passionate professor who wants her students to do well. She cares about making your grade holistic and not just based on tests. Tests are easy if you prepare correctly and utilize her resources (past tests/quizzes/notes). I wish all b-school professors were like her!
Take Dr. Austin. She cares about the students and runs the class in an organized fashion.

I dont know why Dr Austin has such a bad review. Austin takes a relatively boring topic and makes the class fun and engaging. Her energy is unmatched and while the tests and projects may take a little effort, they are very fair. If you put in effort youll do fine in the class. Take her class.

Shes fair. Her old reviews are a bit too harsh. She provides all the materials you need, and you will be tested on ANYTHING mentioned in class or on the PowerPoints. So, pay close attention. Worst part of class was the A/C being broken in the room we used. I though accounting was boring at room temp but its even worse at 80 degrees.

Dr. Austin has some bad reviews from a few years ago, but I found her to be a really great professor. Her grading criteria was very clear, and she was always very nice. She is clearly enthusiastic about her class, and though this is overwhelming at times, it makes the boring subjects more bearable. I really enjoyed her and her class!
Super easy, kind lady, seems to care a lot. overall pretty good teacher

Great prof, super sweet. There are a few tests (no surprises), a few quizzes, a project, and a few large HWs, so there are lots of ways to lift up a grade. She is super nice and caring, and is available to help students. I also learned some good Excel/Tableau skills that I used at my internship, so it is worth it to take the class. Def recommend.

This was her first semester teaching AIS(Spring 2018). 2 difficult multiple choice quizzes. Goes through lecture VERY quickly then its on your own working on computer (excel, access) with some assistance from her. Midterm was tough. Lots of projects outside of class (usually difficult)

Professor Austin takes a boring subject and makes the most of it. If you give the class effort and keep up with weekly homework then it should be a breeze. She really walks you through everything you need to know and gives you every chance to get an A

The tests are hard. You do not need a book for her ACC202 class and you almost don't need to be in class since she puts all the powerpoints online and just reads off of them in class. Very fast paced and she rushes through the slides so you don't have time to actually learn the material. Nice woman, tries to make it entertaining, but tough class.

Shout out to ratemyprofessor for not allowing a zero! yall are at least sympathetic to grades. Basic new B school teacher trying to at act as if she is an amazing teacher by making class super hard. She wants to be like professor Hoyle but she's far away from that. Avoid at all costs, you will fail the final, she made it like this. Horrible overall

She's the worst. One of the fakest professors I've ever had. Her kindness is all on the surface. She really only has one way of teaching accounting and if you can't understand the one specific way she teaches then you're in trouble. The final is also way too hard and she told us that she's purposely made it hard for all of us, thanks Ash!

Honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had here. Tries to come off as this really sweet, caring professor, but once you get to really know her, you figure out that she could care less about her students. Lectures go way too fast and when we told her this, she couldn't have cared less what we thought. Purposely makes the final really hard.

She goes through the PowerPoint so fast it is impossible to take notes. I got an A in financial and barely scrapped by in this class. I showed up to class every single time, went to office hours and studied for five hours or more for each exam. She does not know how to teach if its not how she taught it the first time. Very difficult to do well.
Loved the engaging and interactive classroom activities. Makes learning accounting fun.

Professor Austin is so sweet and works very hard to make the class interesting for those who are not necessarily be interested in accounting. Her grading is fair and she only tests information included in her lectures/powerpoints. Didn't have to buy the textbook because she explained things well in class and had good example problems
